title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the marginal detection benefit of automated sandboxed emulation over a strong deterministic validator for LLM-produced intent→configuration artifacts. Using the declared model (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. Deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results fall well below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, execution accounting diagnostics, an artifact-grounded explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise reproducibility pointers to the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate operator intent into executable network configurations and operational workflows. Operational trustworthiness of such pipelines depends not only on model quality but also on external tooling: deterministic validators, formal verifiers, and sandboxed emulation can detect or reveal configuration errors before production application. Prior work documents generate→validate→repair patterns and prototype runtime emulation for NetOps [1], [2], but quantitative estimates of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation over a capable static validator across multiple vendor-CLI families are scarce. We therefore asked the confirmatory research question that we preregistered: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation?
sections.related_work: Surveys and architectural treatments of LLMs for NetOps and AIOps emphasize workflow-centred mitigations—static validators, formal analysis, and runtime sandboxing—to reduce risk [1], [2]. Tool reports and verification transfers (Batfish/NetKAT, verification-aided compilers) show that dynamic or formal checks can expose runtime failures missed by simple static parsing in some domains [3]. Empirical studies in related code- and config-generation domains demonstrate that external verifiers or emulators can improve correctness, but also that model-generated artifacts often conform to typical templates and can be covered well by targeted validators [4], [5]. This prior literature motivates a paired workflow measurement rather than another model leaderboard: the relevant operational question is how much additional error-detection a guarded (emulation) stage contributes beyond a high-coverage validator for intent→configuration outputs.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. We preregistered a machine-readable plan (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) and froze a paired-binary design with shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under the preregistration the same single sampled initial candidate was reused by both baseline and guarded pipelines for each pair; therefore any between-condition discordance can arise only from (i) guarded-stage emulation observations that reveal violations not encoded in the static validator, or (ii) a permitted repair-stage invocation recorded in the run accounting. Planned confirmatory Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration specified a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 (20 percentage points) targeted for ≈80% power under conservative baseline assumptions. The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution and primary outcome. Execution completed per the preregistration: completed_episode_count = 1440 (complete_pair_count = 720) and model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared_initial generations + 1 repair-stage call). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These values are verbatim from the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor and supporting CSV artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). The analysis input-results SHA-256 is df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8 (execution/raw_results.jsonl).
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded explanation for the negligible guarded benefit. The archived artifacts support three primary, mutually reinforcing factors. (1) Validator ceiling effect: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 achieved near-universal coverage for the curated synthetic task bank (baseline success rate ≈99.861%). Per-episode validator traces show validator_version = 5.0 and violation_count = 0 for the overwhelming majority of confirmatory items, consistent with a ceiling. (2) Task curation and inclusion rules: confirmatory items were parser-validated synthetic tasks designed to exercise workflow patterns but not adversarially engineered to evade the validator; inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance and no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred. (3) Paired/shared_initial_candidate semantics and run accounting: identical initial candidates across conditions restrict discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage emulation observations or the single recorded repair-stage invocation (stage_counts record: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1). Together these factors explain why only a single discordant guarded‑only detection (n10 = 1) occurred across 720 pairs, producing an aggregate effect orders of magnitude below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator to the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic intent→configuration tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline provided a vanishing aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation aligning with the single guarded-only detection. The results are artifact-grounded and constrained: they demonstrate that, in regimes where a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs conform to expected parser patterns, guarded sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at the aggregate level. We emphasize that this conclusion is narrow: in noisier, adversarial, multi-vendor, or stateful operational regimes a guarded stage and higher-fidelity emulation can still provide substantial added detection value. We recommend targeted follow-up experiments using adversarial or cross‑vendor task banks and multiple validator families to identify regimes where guarded stages materially improve operational safety.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and created a validator ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisy, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the execution manifest and provider_call_audit artifacts.
